blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (API tokens are stored in clear in the database) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-security-2 (The Authorization header, and so every bearer token, is written to the logs) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The `api_tokens` table holds `user_id`, `token` and `created_at`; the
middleware looks a request's token up with `WHERE token = $1`. Storing the
token as given keeps the lookup a simple indexed equality.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Tokens are stored as given
findings.recommendation: Store only a hash of the token (SHA-256 is enough for a 32-byte random value, no salt or slow hash needed) and look it up with `WHERE token_hash = $1` on the hash of the presented token; the lookup stays an indexed equality. Anyone who reads the table (backup, replica, SQL injection elsewhere, DBA) otherwise holds working credentials for every user (CWE-312, CWE-256).
findings.title: API tokens are stored in clear in the database

findings.evidence:
To diagnose integration problems, the middleware logs each request's
method, path and headers at `info` level, including `Authorization`, so
support can see which token an integration sent.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Every request is logged with its headers
findings.recommendation: Redact `Authorization` (and `Cookie`) before logging; to let support identify a token, log a non-secret identifier such as the token's id or a short prefix of its hash. Anyone with log access can otherwise replay any integration's token and act as its user (CWE-532). Task 1.3 `logs_requests` should assert the header is redacted.
findings.title: The Authorization header, and so every bearer token, is written to the logs

findings.evidence: - Users create and revoke personal API tokens.
findings.recommendation: Add a requirement and scenario in `specs/api-tokens/spec.md` that a user revokes one of their own tokens and a revoked token gets 401, with the ownership check on the revoke operation (CWE-862), and a task in `tasks.md` to implement and test it. Without it a leaked token stays valid forever, while the design's only risk mitigation relies on revoking it.
findings.title: Revocation is announced but neither specified nor planned
